subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - AcmeFin
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sam Carter <sam.carter@acmefin.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - AcmeFin

Sam / Priya - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call (high-level + next steps) so we have a shared record. Please flag anything I missed or got wrong.

High-level goal
- Reduce unit cost and vendor lock while retaining or improving response quality for our customer-facing assistant and search features.

Pain points you shared
- Rising costs with current OpenAI spend (chat + embeddings) - ~45% of infra budget for this product line.
- Hard dependency on feature parity (function-calling, streaming, embeddings API) - migration needs to be minimally disruptive.
- Latency sensitivity for short-turn interactions (p50 target <300ms, p90 <1s) and strict PII/data residency needs for EU customers.
- Embeddings/retrieval pipeline tied to vector DB (we noted Pinecone today) and current tokenization assumptions.
- Occasional quality regressions (hallucinations) on product recommendations; you want parity or better on hallucination rate for top-5 results.

Current stack (what you confirmed)
- OpenAI: chat completions + function calling for assistant (gpt-4.1-range usage pattern).
- Anthropic: used for safety/secondary assist workflows (low volume).
- Embeddings: OpenAI embeddings -> stored in Pinecone for semantic search + RAG.
- Orchestration: internal batching service, custom retry logic, caching layer (Redis).

Success criteria for a migration PoC
- Cost: >=20% reduction in per-request inference cost at pilot scale.
- Latency: maintain p50 <300ms and p90 <1s for typical assistant requests when run against candidate models on comparable infra.
- Quality: no measurable drop in top-5 precision for recommendation prompts; hallucination rate <= current baseline.
- Compatibility: basic coverage for chat-style completions, streaming, function-calling or a clear adapter path, and an embeddings endpoint compatible with your vector pipeline.

Model shortlist we discussed (initial candidates)
- Llama 2 / Llama 3 family (fine-tune/quantize options)
- Mistral-instruct variants (7B/12B where applicable)
- Falcon / open-source 40B instruct variants (where latency/cost tradeoffs fit)
- Mosaic MPT-30B as a mid-range candidate for embeddings + completions testing

Initial technical risks
- Tokenizer differences for some open models vs. OpenAI -> impacts prompt sizing and cost estimates.
- Function-calling parity: will likely require an adapter layer during PoC.
- Embeddings quality drift: we should benchmark against a fixed evaluation set.

Immediate next steps
1) You to share: current monthly token/embedding usage by endpoint (you mentioned you could export a 30-day summary) and any non-disclosure constraints. (Attachment: acmefin-current-usage.xlsx)
2) Redwood to provide: a short compatibility checklist and PoC proposal (2-week pilot, testing 2 candidate models + embeddings) and a draft SOW/PoC plan for review.
3) Schedule: propose follow-up on Nov 12 to lock model candidates and test dataset.

Attachments: acmefin-current-usage.xlsx (usage export we referenced)

Thanks - I’ll send a PoC outline by tomorrow and a calendar invite for Nov 12.

-
Aditya Rao

Thanks Aditya - this is great and captures the call. Couple quick clarifications:
- Usage: we'll export the last 30 days from billing but FYI the majority of token spend (~70%) is from chat/completions, embeddings are ~25%, rest is small. Expect the spreadsheet by EOD tomorrow.
- Region: EU residency applies to a small subset of enterprise customers (about 12% of traffic) - would like a VPC/private option for that subset.
- Function calling: we rely on it for structured outputs; if an adapter is needed that's fine as long as latency impact is minimal.

Agree on Nov 12 follow-up. Also attaching the SOC/Security questionnaire - we’ll need responses for procurement.

Attachment: acmefin-security-questions.pdf

-
Sam

Marissa / Rishi - forwarding the AcmeFin thread. They sent the security questionnaire and asked for a VPC/private option for EU customers. Key asks for the PoC:
- Run 2 candidate models (we should pick 1 smaller low-latency model and 1 mid-size stronger-quality model).
- Provide embeddings benchmark on their evaluation set (we’ll need to map tokenizers).
- Provide a short adapter plan for function-calling parity.

Attachments they sent: acmefin-security-questions.pdf (forwarded)

Can you two draft the PoC SOW and call out infra recommendations (Dedicated vs Private for the EU subset) + estimated pilot cost? I’ll own scheduling and commercial ask.

Thanks - meeting scheduled Nov 12 10:00am PT (I’ll send invite)

-
Aditya
